scoring_justification: The inverted functions are deterministically computable from public experimental data and fcc Möbius inversion coefficients; the checker recomputes every row of the CSV against the same formulas and coefficients.

hidden_assets.purpose: Experimental data (a0, C12, C44, Es, Ev, B) for Cu, Ag, Au from Foiles et al. (1986) used to compute α, n_e and the functional forms.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Foiles, S.M., Baskes, M.I., Daw, M.S., Phys. Rev. B 33, 7983 (1986) – values as cited in the paper.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Direct extraction from the reference; units converted to eV and GPa as in the paper.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the actual published values the paper uses; substituting different numbers would break the reproduction target.

hidden_assets.purpose: fcc shell weights w(n) for n=1..100, used to compute the Möbius transform m(n).
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Standard fcc lattice neighbour‑shell counts; generated by enumerating all positions with i+j+k even and computing N = (i^2+j^2+k^2)/2.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Algorithmic enumeration up to n=100; matches the provided mobius_coeffs.json resource.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: The checker must use the same w(n) as the agent's inversion to guarantee consistency; the array is computed from the lattice geometry, not invented.

outputs.description: CSV with 300 rows (100 per metal) of inverted hopping integrals and pair potentials as functions of nearest-neighbour distance R1 for Cu, Ag, Au.

output_contract.notes: The deterministic procedure allows the checker to recompute the gold values using the same formulas and public data, comparing each row of the CSV within a tight tolerance. Process steps are required intermediates; their evidence is not scored.

steps.description: Recompute hopping integral and pair potential for all 300 rows from embedded experimental data and fcc Möbius inversion; score by mean relative error within tolerance 1e-5.
